newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish NFI Piast 1996 loss rises to PLN 31.3 mln.
newsitem.headline: Polish NFI Piast 1996 loss rises to PLN 31.3 mln.

text.p: The net loss of National Investment Fund (NFI) No. 12, or Piast, of Poland's mass privatisation scheme rose to 31.3 million zlotys last year from 10.1 million in 1995, the fund said in a issue prospectus.
The fund said its strategy would be to focus on companies in automotive, chemical and textile industries. It would place two firms in its portfolio on the Warsaw Stock Exchange in the next two years.
Under the government's NFI programme, shares in about 500 mid-sized companies are allocated to 15 NFIs run by foreign and domestic management firms.

From May 12 the 26 million Poles who each bought one participation unit in the scheme will have the opportunity to exchange them for 15 shares, one in each fund, which are expected to start trading on the Warsaw bourse around mid-year.
Each NFI has 31,026,185 shares. The units lose their validity on December 31, 1998.
